newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian government agrees 1997 budget review-radio.
newsitem.headline: Belgian government agrees 1997 budget review-radio.

text.p: The Belgian government on Saturday reached provisional agreement on a review of its 1997 budget, Belgian radio said.
Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene's spokeswoman declined to confirm an agreement had been reached and said talks were still continuing.
BRTN radio said ministers had decided on 12 billion francs ($342 million) of new austerity measures to keep the deficit on its target of 2.9 percent of GDP.
It said the measures include a 1.5 billion franc tax on the electricity sector and a two billion franc turnover tax on the pharmaceutical industry, BRTN said.

New income tax prepayments for independent workers must raise one billion francs and sharper control on value added tax-evasion two billion francs. Several ministries, including defence and development cooperation, will have their budgets cut by three to four billion francs, the radio said.

Talks on the budget and on a review of the centre-left government's policy agreement will continue all weekend and Monday. Dehaene is set to address parliament about it on Tuesday. $1 = 34.81 Belgian francs
